pages.transcription:
Petropolis, 10.I.42
My dear Mamma,
From what I hear from my sister-in-law Eva has
had such busy Christmas holidays that I am afraid she has ~~had~~
little time to write you about it. So I report what I know about it:
Salmon's have had her for the whole vacation time and my sister-
in-law and Stefans first wife (please remember the names Ste-
fanie and Friderike, so as to spare me those long words) who wanted to
invite her had to make later appointments. One day she spent at
Mrs. Wiener's and today, I believe, Stefanie takes her to the Opera.- I
am glad for Eva and for you that she has a lovely vacation
time, being taken out, petted and spoiled, and she was greatly
looking forward to 'great fun' at Salmon's. So far I know only
that there was a Christmas party of 18 children in New Rochelle.
Personally I am glad, too, that Wiener's invited her again, not because
they live on Park Avenue - you know that I am indifferent against
such things - but because they love and understand children and
because I like them both. - I hope you have spent pleasant
Christmas days, or better weeks, at Rosemount, and that on the whole
everything is going as you want it to go.- About our life I must so
far repeat the same story again and again: It is raining almost
constantly and that is why the season is very bad and hardly any
of our friends are up here yet. So we continue our quiet life,
having company by our dog and going for walks whenever the
rain stops for a few hours. The description of our walks I leave
to Stefan. It is clearly his job, being a writer to give you an idea
how 10 minutes from the town, one can be in midst almost complete
wilderness and primitive life, in some lonely valley with beautiful
and varied views and lots of children around poor little huts. Need-
less to say that where we go, none of our friends has ever set foot.
- Next week there is the great Pan-American conference in Rio, but the
Brazilians have been so spoilt with attention and visitors this last
year that they don't get very excited about it. - The communications
with USA continue as before, only letters take longer, and so I hope
that the cardigan I knitted for Eva and which I dispatch Monday,
will arrive in due time (and that it will fit). Working at it I thought
of all the knitting we have done together and wished I could have you
here. Also the fog which frequently surrounds us and all the English
woollens I am wearing on account of it, bring back many memories.
Well one day we will talk about all this again. Fortunately time
really flies and soon we will have to think again what to do when our
contract expires in May. I suppose we shall try to remain in this little place
which for our needs has many advantages. - Don't forget to write us a lot!
Fondest love, Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Tinte ist dunkelblau/schwarz, gut lesbar.
Dies ist eine Kopie der ersten Seite mit aufgelegten Archivierungshilfen (Farbskala/Grauskala #13). Der Text ist identisch mit Seite 1.
